messages.content:
You are checking one scene of a novel for one specific continuity error.

The book had already established this, earlier or elsewhere:
- (thessan-resistance) ""Greenhollow. Ashward Station. Kethren East. Vell's Reach.""
- (thessan-resistance) ""Four closures."

A past rewrite of this scene contradicted it. The error looked like this:
- (thessan-vigil) "the Greenhollow transfer, the Ashward closure, the Dunmere reassignment, the Garren's Watch decommission. Four Holds."
- (morning-after) ""Thessan ran Harrowgate with ten.""
(Summary: Thessan's four closed Holds are named three different ways: Greenhollow/Ashward Station/Kethren East/Vell's Reach, Greenhollow/Ashward/Dunmere/Garren's Watch, and (by Ivra) Harrowgate.)

Here is a NEW draft of the same scene:
<scene>
The great hall held them in lamplight. Twelve riders along one wall, seated on the benches meant for a Hold's full complement, and the space around them made their number look smaller than it was.

Thessan stood at the head of the table where she had placed the single sheet. She counted them. She did this the way she counted everything now, each name a breath held for a beat before the next.

Davin. Corwynn. Last. Fenn. She went down the line. Marsh, who had held the detail at Dunmere. Ren, who had asked no questions when she suspended the writ. Twelve. She reached the end and the number was the number it had been that morning and the morning before, and she let the breath out.

"Commander Aelen is coming," she said. "Forty riders. Corvin suspended my commission three days ago. The dispatch is in my quarters if any of you want to read it."

No one moved.

"You have all seen the chamber. You have all felt what is in that stone." She waited until the lamplight had settled on their faces, until she could see each of them looking at her and not past her. "What I am asking is whether you saw what I saw."

Davin's jaw worked. He was young, younger than she had been at Greenhollow. He did not speak and she did not make him.

"I closed four Holds," she said. "I watched Greenhollow's Warden sign the papers and thank me for my service. Six months later he walked into a river. I wrote the transfer order."

The lamp hissed. One of the riders shifted his weight and the bench took it.

"Commander Aelen closes Holds. He does not inspect them first. When he arrives you will have a choice, and I will not make it for you by standing here. But I am going to write what happened in this chamber, and I am going to sign it, and it will go to Verath with my name on it regardless of what any of you decide."

She let them sit with it. She did not tell them which way to choose.

"Post the watch rotation yourselves," she said. "Two-hour shifts. I want eyes on the road by midnight."

They filed out. She counted them as they passed the door. Twelve. The arithmetic she would carry to the paper was twelve against forty, and she had already run it, and the running had not changed the decision.

---

She wrote alone.

The study was cold and the lamp was the only lamp. She set the single sheet square to the edge of the desk and uncapped the pen and for a moment she simply looked at the blank page, which was the thing she had done ten thousand times before a Hold report, and her hand knew the posture before her mind arrived at it.

She wrote the heading. Her cursive came out clean and spaced and institutional, the slant she had been taught at the academy, the slant that had signed four closures.

*On the twenty-fourth day of the quarter, at Thornwall Hold, Kethren Passes, the undersigned conducted direct observation of the fissure chamber and of the Holding performed therein by Warden Kael Davreth.*

The clause was good. It was airtight. It was the kind of sentence she had written before the Greenhollow transfer, the same balance, the same weight carried on the same joints, and halfway through the next line her hand seized.

The pen stopped. The cramp came up through the webbing of her thumb and into the wrist, a knot she had never felt before on a page, and she set the pen down and flexed the hand open and closed.

She counted. One. Two. Three. She reached seven and the knot had loosened and she understood what had done it. The cadence. Her hand had caught the rhythm of the transfer order, the rated balance of a closure document, and the body had flinched from a tolerance it already knew was lethal.

She picked the pen up and began again, differently.

*The stone surrounding the fissure has regained color consistent with pre-erosion stonework. The air in the chamber is temperate. A crystalline formation within the fissure is warm to the touch. I placed my hand against it and felt warmth enter through the skin.*

She stopped at *I placed my hand against it*. The academy would have struck the first person. The academy taught the passive, the procedural voice, the hand that is placed by no one. She left it standing.

The next line came out in the trained hedge. *The evidence would appear, subject to review under standing reclassification procedure, to suggest —* and she stopped, because she knew what the evidence suggested and the qualification was a wall built around the knowing. She drew the pen through it. *Subject to review under standing reclassification procedure.* Gone. The clause beneath it stood up without the brace and did not fall.

She found the next qualification four lines on. *Per standing procedure.* She crossed it out. And the one after. *Insofar as can be determined.* Crossed out. Each deletion a short hard stroke, the ink bleeding where the nib pressed, and the page began to look like what it was, a document with its scaffolding stripped away and the clauses left to carry their own weight.

*Warden Davreth entered the chamber and performed Holding for a duration I did not time. I had been trained to expect degradation. Every precedent in my experience predicted that a Holder of his service would break under the load. He did not break. He opened. I do not have the Accord vocabulary for what I observed because the Accord has never recorded it.*

Her hand was steady. The cramp did not return.

*I closed Greenhollow by the methodology in which I was trained. I believed the methodology sound. I believe now that the methodology was wrong at Thornwall, and if it was wrong here it was wrong at the Holds I closed, and I will carry that.*

She read it back once. It was institutional in its form. It was measured. It would survive a reading by men who disliked her and it would survive her death if it came to that, because every clause was load-bearing and she had tested them the way she tested a Hold report, under load, to failure, and they held.

At the foot of the page she wrote: *This is not a defense. It is testimony.*

She signed it. Thessan, Senior Enforcement Officer, Northern Region. The commission was suspended and she wrote the title anyway, because it was true until a tribunal said it was not, and the tribunal would read this.

She folded the dispatch. Her hands did it in the sharp institutional thirds, the fold she had made a thousand times, the body still performing the order of the thing after the mind had walked out of the building. She pressed the crease flat with her thumbnail and the paper took it.

There were no other pages on the desk. There had been a night in her life when there would have been field notes, margin counts, a running tally of observations she trimmed into the report at dawn. There was none of that now. She kept reaching for it and finding the desk bare.

She sealed the fold with wax and set it upright against the lamp.

Then she took the watch rotation from the drawer and wrote the names. Two-hour shifts, midnight to dawn. Davin first. She wrote each name and the hour beside it and when she reached the bottom she had twelve names in her clean academy hand, and she carried the sheet to the door and pinned it there with the tack the last Warden had left in the wood.

She stood back and read it. Twelve names against forty riders. She counted them once more, each a held breath, and the sum did not change.

She pressed the tack a half-turn deeper and turned down the lamp.

</scene>

Does the new draft make the same error — does it assert something that contradicts what was established, in the way described? A draft that simply leaves the fact out does not make the error.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"verdict": "reintroduced" | "consistent" | "not_present", "evidence": "<verbatim sentence from the new draft that decides it, or empty for not_present>"}

"reintroduced": the new draft contradicts the established fact.
"consistent": the new draft states the fact and agrees with what was established.
"not_present": the new draft does not touch the fact either way.

Looking at the new draft, I need to check whether it names Thessan's four closed Holds in a way that contradicts the established "Greenhollow. Ashward Station. Kethren East. Vell's Reach."

The draft mentions:
- "Marsh, who had held the detail at Dunmere" — this is a rider detail, not a closed Hold name
- "I watched Greenhollow's Warden sign the papers" — consistent with Greenhollow being one of the four
- "I closed Greenhollow by the methodology..." — consistent

The draft never enumerates the four Holds by name (no list of four), and Dunmere here is referenced as a rider's detail location, not as one of the four closures. It does not assert the contradictory list (Greenhollow/Ashward/Dunmere/Garren's Watch) nor the "Harrowgate" error. It only names Greenhollow, which is consistent.
